title: Exploring the association between housing insecurity and mental health among renters: A systematic review of quantitative primary and secondary studies
summary: A systematic review of studies from OECD settings found housing unaffordability and instability among renters often associated with poorer mental-health outcomes. It frames housing conditions as important context, not as personal cognitive errors.
limitations: The review judged certainty of evidence low to very low because most included designs were not controlled. Heterogeneous exposure/outcome measures, an OECD-only adult renter scope, and a search ending in December 2022 constrain broader or causal claims.

title: Prospective Associations of Childhood Housing Insecurity With Anxiety and Depression Symptoms During Childhood and Adulthood
summary: A prospective cohort analysis investigated whether childhood housing insecurity was associated with later anxiety and depression symptom patterns after adjustment for repeated poverty measures, supporting attention to long-term material circumstances.
limitations: Observational cohort from a defined western North Carolina setting and historical follow-up period. It cannot establish that housing insecurity caused an individual's symptoms, predict a person's outcome, or justify retraumatizing housing questions.

title: Precarious employment and mental health in the United States: Results from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), 2008-2021
summary: A nationally representative analysis of employed U.S. adults' MEPS responses found increasing multidimensional employment precarity associated with poorer self-rated mental health. Job security and working conditions are contextual factors, not merely individual coping choices.
limitations: Observational self-reported mental-health outcome; unmeasured confounding and reverse direction remain possible. Excluded unemployed and self-employed workers, so findings should not be generalized to every gig worker or those who have lost jobs.

title: Does persistent precarious employment affect health outcomes among working age adults? A systematic review and meta-analysis
summary: A systematic review examined persistent precarious employment and health, including mental-health outcomes. It links occupational insecurity to a broader structural context for health and labor policy.
limitations: The authors judged the GRADE certainty very low and causality highly uncertain. Employment definitions and follow-up periods varied; this is not evidence that a single worker's distress has one cause or that any specific chatbot intervention helps.

title: The immediate effect of discrimination on mental health: A meta-analytic review of the causal evidence
summary: This meta-analysis of experimental manipulations found adverse immediate mental-health effects from discriminatory experiences, complementing observational discrimination literature and challenging explanations that place all distress inside the individual.
limitations: Laboratory manipulations do not reproduce the chronic exposure, power relations, and harms of real-world discrimination. Convenience sampling, predominantly young and highly educated participants, limited ecological validity, and short-term outcomes restrict generalization.

title: Meta-analysis of the effect of racial discrimination on suicidality
summary: A meta-analysis reported population-level associations between experienced racial discrimination and suicidal ideation and attempts, emphasizing that suicide prevention can involve reducing exposure to discrimination as well as individual support.
limitations: Association is not individual risk prediction, and included studies differ in measures and time horizons. This record must never drive a clinical risk score, presume that demographic identity implies suicidal intent, or replace immediate-risk assessment.

title: Understanding loneliness: a systematic review of the impact of social prescribing initiatives on loneliness

limitations: Only nine eligible studies, nonuniform measures and nonrandom samples, and insufficient reported intervals for meta-analysis. Do not claim a proven intervention effect or substitute an AI relationship for community ties.
